title: Illinois Condominium — Governance, Meetings & Elections
help: Statewide Illinois condominium governance infrastructure. Statutory board, meeting, notice, election, voting, vacancy, and rule-adoption requirements are Infrastructure; an association's current directors, officers, meeting calendar, election configuration, and retained references are association-instance data.

scope.label: Illinois statewide condominium infrastructure
scope.admission_rule: Statewide Illinois applicability is required. County-specific, municipal, association-customary, future-effective, or uncertain requirements are deferred until separately modeled.

authorities.summary: Illinois Condominium Property Act bylaw requirements governing boards, meetings, elections, notices, voting, vacancies, quorums, and related governance.
Board powers and duties, including rule-adoption procedure.

pages.title: Governance, Meetings & Elections
pages.help: Current-effective statewide governance rules are separated from association-specific roster, schedule, election, and document references.

sections.title: Statewide governance framework
sections.help: These requirements apply statewide under the Illinois Condominium Property Act.

controls.text: The bylaws must provide for election of a board of managers from among the unit owners, with all board members elected at large; terms of at least one-third of the board must expire annually. If a unit has multiple owners, only one of them may serve on the board at one time.
No board member or officer may be elected for a term longer than 2 years, but board members and officers may succeed themselves.
The board must meet at least 4 times annually.
The members must hold an annual meeting, one purpose of which is election of members of the board of managers.
Special meetings of the members may be called by the president, the board of managers, or 20% of the unit owners.
Written notice of a membership meeting must give members not less than 10 and not more than 30 days notice of the time, place, and purpose, subject to the Act's electronic-transmission provisions.

Notice of every board meeting must generally be posted at least 48 hours before the meeting, and at least 48 hours' notice must also be provided as required by the Act to owners using authorized technological means and, where condominium instruments require, to other owners.

Every board meeting must be open to unit owners except for the limited discussion categories permitted by the Act. Any vote on those matters must occur in a meeting or portion of a meeting open to unit owners.
A unit owner may record proceedings of board meetings, or portions of them, that are required to be open, subject to reasonable board rules governing recording.

Board members may participate in board meetings in person, by telephone, or by acceptable technological means that allow all participants to communicate with each other; such participation constitutes attendance and presence.

Before adopting or amending operational rules and regulations, the board must call a unit-owner meeting for the specific purpose of discussing the proposed rules. The meeting notice must contain the full text of the proposed rules; no quorum is required unless the condominium instruments expressly require one.

The board may not enter certain contracts with a current board member, or with a corporation or partnership in which a board member or immediate family member has at least a 25% interest, unless the statutory notice and owner-petition/election opportunity is provided.

The bylaws must provide a vacancy-filling method that includes temporary board appointment by a two-thirds vote of the remaining board and an owner-petition mechanism under which owners holding 20% of association votes may require a meeting to fill the vacancy.

sections.title: Association governance configuration
sections.help: These values instantiate the statewide framework for a particular association and do not become statewide civic identity.

controls.label: Board quorum
controls.help: Use the association-specific percentage if the bylaws specify something other than a majority.

controls.label: Membership quorum
controls.help: For condominiums with 20 or more units, the statute establishes a 20% default unless the owners holding a majority percentage interest provide for a higher percentage.

controls.label: Governance instrument reference
controls.help: Reference to the bylaws/declaration provisions that instantiate board size, quorum, officer, vacancy, meeting, and election mechanics.

sections.title: Current board and officers
sections.help: Names, offices, terms, and local unit references are association-instance facts.

sections.title: Meeting administration
sections.help: Track association meeting events and retained evidence without hard-coding one notice, calendar, or minutes system.

sections.title: Elections and voting
sections.help: The Act supplies statewide election and voting mechanics while each association records the election method and event-specific dates it actually uses.

controls.text: Voting is generally on a percentage basis using each unit's percentage interest in the common elements, except where the bylaws validly provide one vote per unit for matters for which the Act does not specify the required approval basis.

For board elections, the Act permits proxy voting unless a qualifying declaration, bylaw, or rule provides for association-issued ballot or acceptable-technological-means procedures. Those alternative procedures carry specific candidate-notice and ballot/instruction timing requirements.

item_controls.label: Candidate deadline notice
item_controls.help: For statutory ballot/technology procedures, owners must receive at least 21 days' written notice of the candidacy deadline.
